missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Компьютер' stays in the nominative as the subject of 'стоит'. 'Новый' is the agreeing masculine adjective, and 'на столе' adds the location. A clean model for describing a device.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Компьютер' is an inanimate masculine noun, so its accusative matches the nominative as the direct object of 'купил'. 'Новый' agrees, and 'вчера' fixes the time.
Strategic focus: Genitive of absence. 'Компьютера' takes the genitive after 'нет' to mark non-existence. 'Своего' agrees in the masculine genitive, showing ownership. A core negation pattern.
Strategic focus: Dative with 'к'. 'К компьютеру' uses the dative form 'компьютеру' to show movement toward the device. 'Утром' adds the time of day. A natural motion-toward pattern.

missions.phrase: Я работаю за компьютером весь день.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Instrumental with 'за'. 'За компьютером' uses the instrumental 'компьютером' to mean sitting and working at the machine. 'Весь день' shows duration. A very common everyday phrase.
Strategic focus: Prepositional location. 'На компьютере' uses the prepositional 'компьютере' to mean stored on the machine. 'Много старых файлов' takes the genitive plural after a quantity word.
Strategic focus: Genitive singular after a numeral. After 'три' the noun takes the genitive singular 'компьютера' even though three are meant. 'Дома' sets the place. A key number-noun rule.
Strategic focus: Accusative plural. 'Компьютеры' is the nominative-like accusative plural of an inanimate noun, the object of 'продают'. 'Разные' agrees, and 'в магазине' gives the place.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural subject. 'Компьютеры' is the nominative plural subject of 'работают'. 'Эти' agrees in the plural, and 'очень быстро' describes performance. A clean plural model.
Strategic focus: Genitive with 'без'. 'Без компьютера' uses the genitive 'компьютера' to express working without the device. 'Трудно работать' states the difficulty. A useful preposition pattern.
